title: Technical English — Course 3, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 1

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the introduction begin?
tasks.audioText: The materials laboratory will hold an introduction for new students on Tuesday at nine thirty. The technician will demonstrate how to read material labels and record basic properties. Students should meet outside Laboratory 4 and wear their college identification badges. The session will not include practical testing; that activity will be arranged later.

tasks.prompt: An engineering student compared aluminium and steel for a lightweight support bracket. Aluminium has a lower density, so a component made from it may weigh less. Steel is generally stronger in many common grades, but the exact choice depends on the load, environment and design requirements. The student recorded the material grade and checked the drawing before writing a recommendation. Reading 1. Why did the student consider aluminium?
options: Because aluminium is always stronger than steel
Because it has a lower density and may produce a lighter component
Because it requires no design checks
Because it is suitable for every load and environment

tasks.prompt: What information did the student record?
The aluminium sample is ___ than the steel sample of the same volume.
Choose TWO properties that may be relevant when selecting a material for a bracket.
options: The colour of the workshop door

tasks.prompt: The mass of a material in relation to its volume is its ___.
You need to confirm the material grade shown on a drawing. What is a suitable question?
options: I will use any material without checking.
Could you confirm the material grade specified for this part?
I do not need the specification.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of materials and properties in a logical order.
options: Record the selection and its reason
correctOrder: Record the selection and its reason

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words recommending a material for a simple support bracket. Compare two properties and explain why the drawing and service conditions matter.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); accurate technical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
